dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Select the introducing (oldest) `--diff-filter=A` commit for a `.retired` tombstone (e.g. `--reverse` then take the first, or `--follow`) rather than commits[0] which is the newest addition.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:130:         commits = [line.strip() for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:131:         return commits[0] if commits else None
Docstring/ticket intent: 'resolves the tombstone's folding commit ... the commit that introduced the .retired path' — the introducing commit is the OLDEST addition, but git log lists newest-first.
dropped.finding: `_tombstone_folding_commit` returns `commits[0]` from `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H`, which is reverse-chronological (newest first). The docstring and ticket define the folding commit as the commit that INTRODUCED the `.retired` path, i.e. the oldest/first addition. If the tombstone path was ever added, deleted, and re-added, commits[0] is the most-recent re-addition, not the original folding commit — so eligibility is anchored to the wrong (newer) commit age.
scenarios: A `.retired` tombstone path that was added, later removed, then re-added at a newer commit — commits[0] is the newer re-addition, understating the true age of the folding event.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add `--reverse` to the git log invocation (and keep taking the first line), or take `commits[-1]`, so the earliest addition is chosen as the folding commit.
